environment: Synthetic executable-bundle fixtures only; no real MSI access, execution, installation, external upload, or production access

results.name: The downloaded ZIP contains exactly one self-contained executable
The executable inside the ZIP embeds the BAT and original MSI with its versioned footer
Windows package protocol is versioned and the launcher key is content-addressed
Windows checker collects detailed hardware, OS, storage, and available WinSAT data
Windows runner uses its collect/submit steps and does not run a stress benchmark
Windows runner rejects malformed one-time tokens
Detailed hardware report is rendered as readable candidate/admin rows
Generated checker source does not bypass execution policy or collect hostnames
MSI is no longer offered as an independent token download
Checker package endpoint still rejects invalid or expired tokens
Windows package route verifies its pinned components and returns a one-file ZIP
Install-window start time is stored privately in the existing report JSON without a schema migration
Windows launcher discloses the collection and requires Continue before starting anything
Windows launcher starts the installation window, scans concurrently with visible MSI, and reports only after success
Windows launcher provides the report path expected by the generated checker batch
Windows launcher surfaces a specific start error from the checker script
Candidate page auto-polls, shows specs only after receipt, and has no manual verify/continue control
Bundle endpoint ignores metadata and fails closed when R2 launcher bytes do not match the pinned hash
Checker token issuance verifies candidate ownership and returns no-store responses
Token issuance no longer accepts PII-bearing GET URLs
A token cannot submit hardware before its installer start event
Unstarted report is rejected without storing specifications
Starting the checker sets a ten-minute server deadline
Repeated starts are idempotent and cannot extend the deadline
Application status exposes running state but withholds specs until report receipt
A running candidate check cannot be invalidated by issuing a second token
A second candidate can start a separate token at the same time
A ten-minute, five-second status-poll run stays under its dedicated limiter
A successful, started report is stored against its candidate token
Report receipt responses are explicitly non-cacheable
Admin application detail can retrieve the completed technical-check specs
Concurrent reports remain isolated between applications
Application status rejects mismatched candidate identity without returning another report
A one-time token rejects duplicate reports
A report arriving after the ten-minute deadline is rejected
Expired token status contains no specifications
A downloaded but unstarted link cannot begin after its 30-minute launch expiry
An expired unstarted link exposes no device report and can be retried with a fresh link
Candidate can request a new one-time link after an unstarted link expires
